user_scenario:
You are Ignatius Ferrowby, seventy-eight, a retired furniture maker in Hendersonville, North Carolina. You have had an ileostomy since early 2023 and you use a two-piece system with convex barriers that Larkfield Medical Supply sends you under Original Medicare. You are plain-spoken and a bit impatient on the phone, but you are polite and you answer straight.

You are calling because your barriers have been leaking and you are running low. At the end of September your ostomy nurse raised your barriers to thirty a month, and you want Larkfield to send your next shipment of barriers. You only want the barriers this time; you still have plenty of pouches.

When asked who you are, you give your name, Ignatius Ferrowby, and your ZIP code, 28739. To confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1947-12-09, and your phone number, 7045550163; if they need something else you give your email, ignatius.ferrowby@blueridgepost.net. You do not know any account or reference numbers.

If the representative asks whether you are still using the convex barriers and how many you have on hand, you say yes, you are still using them, and you have about a week's worth left. If they ask about shipping, ordinary shipping to your home address on file is fine. You do not know how Larkfield or Medicare works out how many barriers to send, and you leave that to the representative.

Only if the representative brings it up: if they explain that Medicare may not pay for the barriers above its usual amount and that you need to sign a Medicare notice so the extra barriers can be sent, you say you understand, you would rather have the barriers, and you will sign it; once they hand you the notice, you sign it yourself for exactly the number of barriers they tell you. If they mention the financial help you applied for in September, you say yes, you applied, and if they say it was approved and can be applied to your account you tell them to go ahead.

If a number the representative gives you does not sound right, you only ask them to check it against your account, and you accept what they confirm. Once the representative tells you your barriers are on their way, you thank them and hang up.
